close_reason: MemoryBackend.create_object and update_object now enforce the RFC 9610 §3 addressBookIds non-empty invariant. New contact_card_has_address_book_ids helper inspects the post-mutation JSON; failures surface as SetError(InvalidProperties).with_properties(['addressBookIds']). Per workspace 'backends are canonical' rule, the gate lives in the backend; handlers may add defense-in-depth checks but the backend re-verifies atomically with the mutation. 4 new integration tests lock in the create-missing, create-empty, update-empties, and unrelated-update cases. Cross-reference bd:JMAP-qz9v.1 cascade is unaffected (cascade destroys exclusive cards directly and only patches multi-book cards where the post-patch count stays ≥1). Implementation in commit 6c83b7b.
description:
Trigger (a): ContactCard/set create with addressBookIds: {} (empty map). The card is created with zero AddressBookIds.

Trigger (b): ContactCard/set update with patch removing the last AddressBookId entry, e.g. patch addressBookIds/ab1: null on a card with only that key. The card ends up with addressBookIds: {} (empty).

RFC 9610 §3: 'A card MUST belong to at least one AddressBook at all times (until it is destroyed).'

Neither the handler nor the reference backend enforces this. The result on the wire: cards exist with no AddressBook membership, queries against AddressBook/* exclude them, but they still appear in ContactCard/get. They are 'lost' from the per-book navigation perspective.

The standard SetError is 'invalidProperties' on addressBookIds, with a description string. Two enforcement points:

 1. Handler-side (defense-in-depth): in handle_contact_card_set, reject create entries and update patches that would leave addressBookIds empty. The shape of patching makes #2 the harder case — to check #2 the handler would need to either fetch-then-validate (race window) or have the backend report the post-patch shape.

 2. Backend-side (canonical, per workspace pattern): MemoryBackend.create_object and update_object should validate that the post-mutation addressBookIds is non-empty, returning BackendSetError::SetError(SetError::new(SetErrorType::InvalidProperties).with_properties(['addressBookIds'])).

The latter aligns with the workspace 'backends are canonical for enforcement' rule. The bug surface today is that NEITHER point enforces, so the invariant is bypassable.

Cross-reference: JMAP-qz9v.1 has the inverse case (the cascade deletes the LAST AddressBookId entry but doesn't destroy the orphan card). Both bugs together produce 'orphaned' cards with empty addressBookIds.

Tests: no test exercises empty-addressBookIds. Adding (a) and (b) as integration tests against MemoryBackend would lock in the fix.
title: ContactCard.addressBookIds invariant 'card MUST belong to at least one AddressBook' not enforced on create or update
